data.prompt: Run your `dedupe` function on the list `[1, 0, 1]` and, after each iteration of the outer `for` loop, print the current value of `x` and the current contents of `a`. Observe how many times the loop body executes and what the list looks like when the first duplicate is removed.
data.trace_question: After the first pass where `x` is `1`, what is the value of `a`? Does the outer `for` loop continue to iterate after `a` has become `[1, 0]`?
data.expected_insight: You will see that the loop keeps iterating even after the list has already been reduced to the correct result, because you are mutating the list you are iterating over. This explains why the final output is `[0, 1]` instead of the expected `[1, 0]`.
